meta.title: Window Film and Your HOA in Nevada | BC Glass & Tint
meta.description: Nevada law protects your right to add shutters for energy costs. It does not say the same about window film. Here is what NRS 116.2111 says and how to get film approved.
meta.image_alt: Living room windows looking out to the desert

v3.lede: If your home sits in a community association anywhere in the Las Vegas valley, the question is almost always the same: am I allowed to put film on my windows? Nevada's law answers part of it, and your association's own documents answer the rest. This is not legal advice.

blocks.heading: What NRS 116.2111 says.
blocks.lede: Five provisions of the section of Nevada's Common-Interest Ownership Act that governs alterations to a home inside an association.

items.term: Changing the outside appearance of your home requires the association's permission.
items.detail: An owner may not change the appearance of the common elements, or the exterior appearance of a unit or any other portion of the common-interest community, without permission of the association. Film that is visible from outside falls under that sentence.
items.source: Source: Nevada Revised Statutes 116.2111, subsection 1, paragraph (b).

items.term: Nevada law names four things an association may not unreasonably restrict, and they are a short list.
items.detail: Improvements needed for a resident with a disability; additional locks to improve security; shutters to improve security or to reduce the cost of energy; and a wind energy system where the property is two acres or more.
items.source: Source: Nevada Revised Statutes 116.2111, subsection 2, paragraph (c).

items.term: Window film is not on that list.
items.detail: The words film and tint do not appear anywhere in NRS Chapter 116. That is not a loophole and not a prohibition. It means film is handled by your association's own governing documents.
items.source: Source: Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 116, full chapter text, read 28 August 2026.

items.term: Shutters get a second, stronger protection that film does not get.
items.detail: The statute devotes an entire subsection to shutters, including rolling shutters. Nothing equivalent exists for window film.

items.term: Anything visible has to follow your association's procedure and suit the look of the community.
items.detail: Visible improvements must be installed under the procedures in the association's governing documents and be compatible with the style of the community. In plain terms: fill out the architectural request, and pick a film that does not stand out.

blocks.note: Read the statute yourself: Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 116, section 116.2111.

blocks.heading: What this means when you want film.
paragraphs: An association is rarely objecting to window film as such. It is objecting to a mirrored look that makes one house stand out from the row. The request that gets approved is usually the plain one: a non-reflective film, submitted through architectural review before the work is booked, with the product named.

Tell us up front that your home is in an association. We will give you the film name and finish in writing so you have something concrete to attach to the request. We would rather wait for your approval than install something you have to take off.

blocks.heading: Your association decides.
paragraphs: We cannot tell you what your association will approve, and we will not quote a reflectivity limit for your community. Those numbers live in each association's own design guidelines, they differ, and we have not verified any specific one. Ask your association for its architectural guidelines in writing.
We install window film. We are not attorneys and nothing here is legal advice.

items.question: Do I need HOA approval before tinting my home windows?
items.answer: Assume yes if the film will be visible from outside. Nevada law says an owner may not change the exterior appearance of a unit without permission of the association, so the safe order is: get the film and finish in writing from us, submit your architectural request, then book the install. Source: Nevada Revised Statutes 116.2111, subsection 1, paragraph (b).

items.question: Does Nevada law protect my right to install window film to cut energy costs?
items.answer: Not in the way it protects shutters. NRS 116.2111 bars an association from unreasonably restricting four specific additions, and window film is not among them. Source: Nevada Revised Statutes 116.2111, subsection 2, paragraph (c), and the full chapter text.

items.question: What should I put on the architectural request form?
items.answer: The specific film and its finish, the windows it goes on, and who is installing it. Call or text us and we will put that in writing for you before you submit.

items.question: Do you work inside HOA communities in Henderson and Las Vegas?
items.answer: Yes. For homes we come to you. Our shop is in Boulder City and we work throughout Henderson, Las Vegas and Southern Nevada.
